sectionPlanTemplate.guidance: Draft sections from claims and reader decisions before writing final copy.

sections.sectionClaim: A face can look shiny while also feeling uncomfortably tight; oil and hydration are not interchangeable labels.
sections.evidenceNeeded: Reviewed editorial explanation of oil versus hydration.
sections.exampleOrTradeoff: A reader may blot their nose at midday yet feel tight after cleansing.
sections.caveatOrNotRightForYou: This guide cannot determine the cause of irritation or diagnose a condition.

sections.sectionClaim: A comparison of visible shine and comfort cues helps readers describe what they see without treating it as a test result.
sections.evidenceNeeded: Reviewed organic page patterns and MyMirror visible-signal position.
sections.exampleOrTradeoff: Surface shine can coexist with dullness or rough-feeling areas.
sections.caveatOrNotRightForYou: Do not over-read one day or one product experience.
sections.transitionPurpose: Move to a measured next choice.

sections.sectionClaim: When skin feels off, simplifying is usually a safer first decision than adding many new actives.
sections.evidenceNeeded: Professional care basics and cautious competitor patterns.
sections.exampleOrTradeoff: Keep the routine short enough to notice what feels comfortable before making another change.

sections.sectionClaim: Persistent, painful, rapidly changing, or markedly irritated concerns deserve clinical input rather than online categorisation.
sections.readerQuestion: When is this not a self-care question?
sections.evidenceNeeded: Cleveland Clinic escalation guidance and MyMirror policy.
sections.exampleOrTradeoff: A guide can organise visible signals but cannot assess the underlying reason for a painful rash.
sections.caveatOrNotRightForYou: Do not rely on MyMirror for diagnosis, prescriptions, or urgent assessment.

sections.sectionClaim: A clearer picture can lead to one calm next step.
sections.exampleOrTradeoff: Use the scan to organise visible signals; use a dermatologist for medical assessment.
